{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABZdIYeA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhDEVQY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 33, "title": "Support standard-size Saturn media with sector-addressed HLE bootstrap", "body": "## Problem

Related to #17

At `78d0046df44ab6eae928afbfafd2fb580fb74434`, otherwise supported discs encounter conflicting size restrictions:

- `src/disc.rs:8,142–149` rejects cooked boot images above 16 MiB.
- `src/media.rs:149–156,495–516` limits CUE input to 512 MiB and boot data to 16 MiB. `Media::boot_iso` decodes and copies the entire stored first track before parsing bootstrap metadata.
- `web/app.js:382–401` limits ISO selection to 16 MiB and aggregate CUE selections to 128 MiB, while retaining additional concatenated input copies.
- `src/lib.rs:446–455,795–800` uses whole-track extraction for mixed-media cold boot and guest SYSRES.

These restrictions prevent ordinary disc-sized media from reaching the implemented hardware. Whole-track decoding also makes HLE startup depend on unread sectors outside its bootstrap inputs. Existing small demonstrations do not establish this capability.

## Expected outcome

Admit standard-size cooked ISO and supported BIN/CUE media through native and production browser paths. Parse bootstrap information through checked sector access to the retained medium, reading the system area, descriptor set, required directory records and selected first-read extent without constructing a second complete cooked track.

Keep total medium capacity separate from the first-read file's legal WRAM destination and size. Retain the actual medium for subsequent timed CD commands, XA transfers and CD-DA. Apply the same bootstrap implementation on cold boot and HLE SYSRES.

The primary contract is:

- Disc layout and capacity: [ST-040-R4 §§1.2,1.5–1.6,2.2–2.4](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/ST-040-R4-051795.pdf), with [Technical Bulletin #7, recording range and track-layout corrections](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/Sattechs.pdf#page=9). A generated layout with 60 minutes of data and short audio/gap regions fits comfortably within the published range and exceeds every current byte cap.
- Bootstrap metadata and first-read selection: ST-040-R4 §§3.2,4.1–4.3,4.7; [Technical Bulletin #35, first-read load-area correction](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/Sattechs.pdf#page=113). These describe bootstrap inputs and destination constraints, separately from total disc size.
- Checked volume and extent interpretation: [ECMA-119 second edition §§6.1–6.4,8.4.8,8.4.12,9.1](https://ecma-international.org/wp-content/uploads/ECMA-119_2nd_edition_december_1987.pdf).
- Runtime addressing and transfers: [ST-162 CD Communication Interface §§2.2,3.4,7.2.3,8.2](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/ST-162-062094.pdf).

This is a media-admission/bootstrap increment. Full BIOS initialization, HLE CD-library services, remaining drive timing and other #17 hardware requirements remain outstanding.

## Context and reproduction

Use a generated original Saturn IP/ISO9660 fixture with a small executable and a complete data volume exceeding 16 MiB. Current `Boot::HleDisc` rejects it before guest execution. Represent equivalent bytes as supported CUE data media: `reset_media` rejects its boot track. Larger selections also encounter the browser and CUE aggregate limits above.

Implement a bounded, checked sector-reader interface suited to the existing owned media model. Preserve supported interleaving, extended-attribute offsets, descriptor scanning, area groups and zero first-read behavior. Bootstrap scratch storage must follow required metadata/executable data rather than total track length. Avoid unnecessary full-medium copies across JS/Wasm, bootstrap and reset; no new streaming framework or compression support is required.

Use documented, consistent resource bounds sufficient for the published standard disc envelope, including raw-sector storage and audio. Do not introduce a new 63-minute rejection for media previously accepted by the broader runtime model. Document resource policy separately from hardware limits.

Implementation agents may correct this AI-authored contract using exact primary references and rationale in the source Issue. Such corrections require no human confirmation and must preserve the fixed #17 goal and independent validation.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Native and browser admission support standard-size ISO and supported CUE media beyond the existing 16/128/512 MiB restrictions. Checked sector counts, aggregate lengths, FAD/LBA conversions and allocation failures produce bounded errors without stale execution or silent truncation.
- [ ] Cold boot and HLE SYSRES use sector-addressed bootstrap without whole-track cooked extraction or a temporary duplicate mount. Focused native read observations show that unrelated payload sectors are not decoded. A deliberately damaged unread raw sector permits bootstrap; damage in a required bootstrap sector fails explicitly under the documented boot decode policy.
- [ ] Independent parser vectors cover first-read extents beyond the old 16 MiB boundary, sector-crossing metadata, interleaving, extended attributes, declared-volume bounds, truncation and overflow. Preserve metadata validation and apply the documented first-read load-area correction without treating disc capacity as executable size.
- [ ] Add reproducibly generated, wholly original MIT-licensed media and SH-2 source. Include a 270,000-sector cooked data volume (552,960,000 bytes), equivalent supported CUE coverage with original audio and valid gaps, and raw Mode1/XA regression vectors. Generate large artifacts during validation rather than committing hundreds of megabytes. Record deterministic layout expectations and hashes.
- [ ] The guest boots from a first-read extent beyond the former limit, issues real CD commands for a separately located late sector, transfers its data through the existing device path, handles/acknowledges the relevant interrupt and computes an independently expected result. Mixed-media coverage checks TOC/track addresses and nonzero CD-DA samples against original source data.
- [ ] Native tests execute cold boot and guest SYSRES while retaining correct media, backup bytes and boot-mode behavior. Source-literal, late-sector and omitted-command mutations change or prevent the expected guest result. Existing runtime command/sector/DMA timing assertions remain intact.
- [ ] Production Wasm/headless Chromium tests under `/saturn-rust/` actually select and boot generated standard-size ISO and CUE inputs, execute the guest late-sector checks and exercise the audio route. Test rejected input, reset during pending file reads and subsequent valid selection. Metadata-only mocks do not satisfy successful large-media execution.
- [ ] Preserve external-BIOS/HLE separation, synthetic BIOS fixtures, Star Collector, Prism Courier, Hardware Lab, both digital pads, analog input, backup import/export, focus release and local-file privacy. Update size-limit error expectations to meaningful malformed-input/boundary tests rather than deleting rejection coverage.
- [ ] Pass `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native/Wasm Clippy with warnings denied, all registered fixture/media reproduction checks, `sh scripts/build-web.sh` and the complete extended `npm run test:browser`, with no required skips.
- [ ] Update architecture, setup/UI guidance, conformance entries and a focused validation record with exact primary sections, implementation/test links, observed results and remaining limitations. Do not claim full hardware completion or demonstrated commercial-game compatibility.

## Optional validation

Additional generated layouts near documented recording boundaries and browser allocation instrumentation are useful. No personal firmware, commercial media, physical console, human approval or live Pages inspection is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
